title: Secure and verify Admin achievement APIs

spec.problem: Five Admin achievement endpoints rely on session-only protection, mutation handlers skip CSRF/RBAC at routing, SQL errors/zero-row mutations can be reported as success, and list scanning can silently return incomplete data.

acceptance.text: Anonymous requests to all nine METHOD+PATH achievement and tier endpoints return 401; Admin without content permissions returns 403.
GET endpoints require admin.content.read; POST/PUT/DELETE require admin.content.write and trusted-origin CSRF across the achievement definition and tier routes.
All achievement and tier writes validate input, return accurate not-found responses, persist their results, and write audit entries atomically.
Missing records return 404, payload validation matches the shared achievement/tier schemas, and database/row iteration failures do not produce successful partial responses.
Admin gamification list remains usable from its existing UI caller; all nine API verdicts are individually recorded with headed-browser/session evidence where applicable.
Gamification admin screens render at a 390px viewport without invalid table markup, hydration warnings, console errors, or horizontal overflow.

spec.expected_behavior: Permission-checked reads and CSRF-protected, audited writes with complete database error handling and accurate not-found responses.
spec.observed_behavior: Router registers all five under Admin session only; handlers lack route-level permission/CSRF, mutations ignore affected-row counts/audit, and list ignores row/secondary query errors.
spec.rollback_plan: Revert the isolated AUDIT-142 code commit; no schema migration or canonical content changes are required; disposable fixtures are cleaned by test cleanup.

classification.rationale: Restore achievement API RBAC/CSRF, audited database contracts, and fix Gamification hydration markup discovered by headed acceptance.
